prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1128; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage does not match the story: the dents are on another side and at another height than the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The insured reported a rear-end collision at a traffic signal and said a passenger in the vehicle was complaining of neck pain at the scene. The insured is the named driver on the policy, and the policy was in force at the time of loss.

Entry 2: Police attended and their report lists the claimant as an occupant of the insured vehicle. Two independent witnesses gave statements that the collision happened as the insured described.

Entry 3: Photographs of both vehicles were uploaded to the file by the insured and the other driver's carrier. The other driver's account matches the insured's account of how the impact occurred.

Entry 4: The claimant's counsel has written to advise that the claimant is represented and asked that all contact go through their office. Further contact with the claimant has been directed to counsel from this point.

Entry 5: The claimant's initial medical records describe neck strain with a reported injury that fits the mechanism of a low-speed rear impact. No prior complaints involving the neck or that body area appear in the records obtained so far.

Entry 6: Counsel provided a recorded statement from the claimant, which repeated the same account of the collision given at the scene and during the first call. No changes to the sequence of events or the injury description were noted.

Entry 7: The vehicle appraiser inspected the insured vehicle and found dents on the rear panel that sit lower and on the opposite side from the impact area described in the accounts. The height and location of the damage do not line up with the described collision, and the appraiser has flagged this for review.

Entry 8: Searches of the vehicle history show no earlier claims or damage recorded against the insured vehicle. Nothing in the file suggests any damage existed before the policy's coverage began.

Entry 9: Treatment records show physiotherapy sessions that tapered off over several weeks as the claimant's symptoms improved and then stopped. The course of care is consistent with what is usually expected for this type of injury.

Entry 10: Discussed the appraiser's findings with the supervisor, who asked that the damage mismatch be documented in full and that a second inspection be arranged before any settlement position is taken. The file remains open pending that inspection.
